svg.title: 128 · Conclusions must match the graph’s evidence
svg.desc: Answer A: one statement is supported, the fourth statement. The original source order is preserved. Statement 1, that these are the only greenhouse gases, is not established. Statement 2, describing events after 2015, is not established. Statement 3, comparing effects on climate, is not established. Statement 4 is supported: in the supplied greenhouse-gas emissions bar chart, methane emissions remain lower than carbon dioxide emissions throughout the displayed period, 1990 to 2015. Showing two gases does not establish that only two greenhouse gases exist. Data ending in 2015 do not establish what happened after 2015. Emitted mass alone does not establish which gas has the greater effect on climate, because gases have different warming effects per unit mass and different atmospheric lifetimes. This is an evidence-reading guide, not a new emissions graph.

g.text: 128 · Conclusions must match the graph’s evidence
A valid conclusion must match the gases, dates and quantity shown.
The source graph displays emissions from 1990 to 2015.
A graph showing two gases does not list every greenhouse gas.
The existence of other greenhouse gases is not excluded.
A later trend needs later evidence.
3 · Not established — Greater effect on climate?
Emissions mass is not a direct measure of warming effect.
Gases differ in warming effect per unit mass and lifetime.
Methane emissions are lower than carbon dioxide emissions.
Compare the bars only across the years shown.
Which gases? • Which dates? • Which measured quantity?
No numerical emissions values are added in this teaching guide.
